UnitStatement: New repo-native skills under `skills/` should be created using the skill template.
Skill contracts must conform to the design outcomes in `AGENT_HELPS_HUMANS.md` under `Design Outcomes for Skill Contracts` and requirements R10 and R12.
`AGENT_SKILLMAKER.md` owns skill contract evolution and subsystem governance.
New skills must pass `tools/validation/validate_skill_metadata.py`.
The `SKILL.md` template includes a `name` frontmatter field for the skill name.
The `SKILL.md` template includes a `description` frontmatter field describing what the skill does and when to use it.
The `SKILL.md` template includes an optional `compatibility` frontmatter field for shell or brief compatibility notes.
The `SKILL.md` template includes an optional `allowed-tools` frontmatter field using comma-space delimited command specs.
The `SKILL.md` template includes a `metadata` frontmatter mapping.
Skill metadata includes `chirality-skill-version` with template value `1`.
Skill metadata includes `chirality-task-profile` with template value `NONE`.
A skill document includes a top-level skill-name heading.
The Purpose section states the recurring bounded task supported by the skill.
The Suitable agent shells section includes TASK as a supported shell.
The Suitable agent shells section may record optional brief-shape constraints.
The Inputs section lists required input fields.
The Inputs section lists optional input fields.
The Runtime overrides section documents each override key with meaning, default, and allowed values.
The Tool usage section lists preferred tools by repository path.
The Tool usage section lists optional tools by repository path.
The Tool usage section lists disallowed tools or tool classes.
The Outputs section identifies the artifact produced by the skill.
The Non-negotiable constraints section records constraints that cannot be violated.
The QA expectations section records output validity checks.
Every skill must include `BRIEF_SCHEMA.md`.
`BRIEF_SCHEMA.md` is the dispatch contract the orchestrator must provide in the INIT-TASK brief to invoke the skill through TASK.
When TASK loads a skill through `TaskSkill`, it also loads `BRIEF_SCHEMA.md`.
`BRIEF_SCHEMA.md` documents required brief fields with types, defaults, and examples.
`BRIEF_SCHEMA.md` documents optional fields.
`BRIEF_SCHEMA.md` gives RuntimeOverrides guidance for meaning and allowed values.
`BRIEF_SCHEMA.md` includes recommended `CustomInstructions` content for format-critical defense-in-depth.
`CustomInstructions` carry run-specific reinforcement and do not replace skill hydration.
The contract in `SKILL.md` remains authoritative.
Every skill must include `TOOL_POLICY.md`.
Implicit tool assumptions are a design defect.
`TOOL_POLICY.md` recognizes `## Preferred tool order` as a canonical H2 heading.
`TOOL_POLICY.md` recognizes `## Allowed deterministic tools` as a canonical H2 heading.
`TOOL_POLICY.md` recognizes `## Expected use of reasoning` as a canonical H2 heading.
`TOOL_POLICY.md` recognizes `## Disallowed use` as a canonical H2 heading.
`TOOL_POLICY.md` recognizes `## Write boundary` as a canonical H2 heading.
Under `## Allowed deterministic tools`, `### TASK-enforced` documents tools from `allowed-tools` frontmatter enforced by TASK at load time.
Under `## Allowed deterministic tools`, `### Operationally invoked` documents tools named in the Tool usage body and guided by the agent.
Every skill's `TOOL_POLICY.md` must include `## Allowed deterministic tools` with both H3 subsections, `## Disallowed use`, and `## Write boundary`.
`## Preferred tool order` and `## Expected use of reasoning` may be skipped when no content applies.
Every skill must include `QA_CHECKS.md`.
`QA_CHECKS.md` documents minimum output validity checks.
`QA_CHECKS.md` documents failure reporting expectations.
`QA_CHECKS.md` documents any required evidence or logs.
The `allowed-tools` frontmatter field is consumed by TASK during skill resolution.
The `allowed-tools` frontmatter field must follow the canonical format exactly.
`allowed-tools` entries are delimited by comma-space.
Each `allowed-tools` command spec has the form `<interpreter> <repo-relative-tool-path>:<scope_glob>`.
`allowed-tools` command specs include no flags, no extra arguments, and no commas inside a spec.
The `allowed-tools` interpreter is a single token.
The `allowed-tools` repository-relative tool path is a single token relative to the repository root.
The `allowed-tools` scope glob follows the final colon.
A single allowed deterministic tool is represented as one `allowed-tools` command spec.
Multiple allowed deterministic tools are represented as comma-space separated command specs.
TASK rejects a skill when `allowed-tools` is malformed.
The `allowed-tools` field should be omitted entirely when the skill has no deterministic tool requirements.
A skill folder name should be the `TaskSkill` token used in briefs.
A skill `name` frontmatter value should match the folder name.
Skill folder names should prefer lowercase ASCII using letters, digits, and hyphens only.
After creating or updating a skill, run `python3 tools/validation/validate_skill_metadata.py skills`.
`validate_skill_metadata.py skills` checks all skill folders under `skills`.
To validate a narrower root, point `validate_skill_metadata.py` at that narrower root.
